record.original_question: Does there exist a II_1 factor N with no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras such that the Haar unitaries in N form a unique sequential commutation orbit? And can one choose such an N that also has the Haagerup property?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Does there exist a II1 factor N with no diffuse relative (T) subalgebras and with unique sequential commutation orbit? Is there such an N with additionally the Haagerup property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting and definitions. Let $(M,\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra with separable predual, and let $M^\omega$ denote its tracial ultrapower along a free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb{N}$. A unitary $u\in M$ is called a Haar unitary if $\tau(u^n)=0$ for every nonzero integer $n$. Two Haar unitaries $u,v\in M$ are said to sequentially commute if $[u,v]=0$. Define an equivalence relation $\sim$ on the set of Haar unitaries of $M$ by declaring $u\sim v$ if there exist Haar unitaries $w_0=u, w_1,\dots,w_n=v$ in the ultrapower $M^\omega$ such that $w_i$ and $w_{i+1}$ commute for each $0\le i<n$. The equivalence classes are called sequential commutation orbits. One says $M$ has unique sequential commutation orbit if all Haar unitaries of $M$ lie in a single such orbit.

A diffuse von Neumann subalgebra $B\subseteq M$ is said to have the relative property (T) (in the sense of Popa) inside $M$ if every sequence of unital, completely positive, trace-preserving, $B$-bimodular maps $\Phi_n:M\to M$ that converges to the identity pointwise in $\|\cdot\|_2$ does so uniformly on the unit ball of $B$. The II$_1$ factor $M$ has the Haagerup property if there exists a sequence of unital, completely positive, trace-preserving maps $\Phi_n:M\to M$ that are compact relative to $\tau$ and converge to the identity pointwise in $\|\cdot\|_2$.

Question. (a) Does there exist a II$_1$ factor $N$ with separable predual such that $N$ contains no diffuse subalgebra with the relative property (T) and such that the Haar unitaries of $N$ form a single sequential commutation orbit?

(b) Can such an $N$ in addition be chosen to have the Haagerup property?
artifact.status_search_result: The sequential commutation framework was introduced recently and the question of whether a II$_1$ factor with no diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras (in particular one with the Haagerup property) can have a unique sequential commutation orbit appears as an explicitly stated open problem in the current literature on the subject. No solution has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Sequential commutation in tracial von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Defines a Borel equivalence relation on Haar unitaries via finite paths of commuting Haar unitaries in the ultrapower; shows the relation admits either one orbit or uncountably many.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework but leaves open the existence of factors without diffuse relative-(T) subalgebras (and with Haagerup property) that have a unique orbit.

status_evidence.title: Internal sequential commutation and single generation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an internal description of the sequential commutation equivalence relation and applications to single generation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on the same equivalence relation that does not resolve the relative-(T)/Haagerup version of the unique-orbit question.
